items.prompt:
Thank you for taking part in this survey about artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems that can perform tasks previously thought to need human intelligence, such as understanding language, making decisions and recognising complex patterns.

The survey takes about 15 minutes. There are no right or wrong answers. We want to know what you think, whatever your level of interest in the subject.

What is involved: you will answer questions about your views on a range of topics, read one short text, and answer questions about it.

Your rights: taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any time by closing the window. Your answers are anonymous and no identifying information is collected beyond your panel ID, which is used only to arrange your payment and is deleted when the study closes.

Risks and benefits: there are no anticipated risks beyond those of everyday life. Your answers help build a public, freely available picture of how people in {country_name} think about AI.

Data use: anonymised data will be published openly so that researchers, journalists and organisations can use it. No individual can be identified from the published data.

Who is running the study: Common Signals, an independent, non-partisan research organisation. Questions can be sent to hello@commonsignals.org or via the panel messaging system.

By clicking "I agree" you confirm you are 18 or over and consent to take part.
items.notes: Terminate screens to screen-out flow if disagree.

items.prompt: How much do you agree or disagree with each of the following statements?

rows.label: Most people can be trusted.
People who run big institutions such as governments, large companies and the media generally have ordinary people's interests at heart.
The world is becoming a more dangerous place.
The way things are going, my children's generation will have a worse life than mine.
New ideas and ways of doing things are usually better than the old ones.
It is important to protect traditions and ways of life that have served us well.
Society works best when people respect authority and follow the rules.
People should be free to live as they choose, as long as they do not harm others.
The gap between the richest and everyone else is one of the biggest problems facing the country.
People who work hard generally get what they deserve.
Ordinary people like me have little say in what the government does.
When I set my mind to something, I usually manage to make it happen.
Scientific experts usually know better than the general public what is good for society.
Big technology companies have too much power over our lives.
Technological progress has done more good than harm over the past fifty years.
I feel a strong sense of belonging to my local community.
I am proud to be {nationality}.
We have a responsibility to the people who will live long after we are gone.
Big changes in society usually end up benefiting people like me.
I usually feel that I understand what is going on in the news.

items.prompt: How concerned are you about each of the following? Please answer whether or not you have heard much about it before.

rows.label: AI taking people's jobs
Fake videos, images and news made with AI
AI systems treating some groups of people unfairly
AI being used to watch and track people
Children forming relationships with AI chatbots
A small number of companies controlling powerful AI
AI being used in weapons and warfare
AI being used to help make dangerous weapons, such as bioweapons
AI systems becoming more capable than humans and acting outside our control
The energy and water used by AI data centres

items.notes: Balanced deliberately: five present-day harms, two structural/security items, two catastrophic-risk items, one environmental item. Wording avoids field jargon (alignment, x-risk, algorithmic bias); check every label against the Common Signals glossary before fielding.

items.prompt: If a political party made addressing the risks of AI one of its main priorities, would that change how likely you would be to vote for them?

Below is a link to an open letter calling for independent safety testing of powerful AI systems before they are released. If you would like to add your name, click the link, which opens in a new tab, then return here to finish the survey. Please finish the survey first so that your answers are saved.
items.notes: OPEN DESIGN QUESTION: no neutral, real open letter has been identified yet that both perspectives in the field would accept, and the letter must not be hosted by or attributed to Common Signals. Per the instrument's own instruction ("keep it if a neutral letter exists; otherwise drop it rather than fabricate one"), F10 is implemented as disabled/hidden by default (link_url is null) until the research team supplies a real URL in this field. F10_click is recorded only if a link is present and clicked.

items.prompt: If you could ask the people building AI one question, what would it be?

Thank you. The text you read earlier was one of several short texts written for this study, each presenting a different way of talking about AI. Some respondents read a text unrelated to AI. The texts were written by the research team and drew on published sources; none was produced by or for an AI company, campaign group or political party. We are studying how different ways of explaining AI land with different people, so that those who talk about AI in public can do it more accurately and more fairly.

Results will be published free at commonsignals.org. If you have any questions about the study, contact hello@commonsignals.org.
